diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given $\underline{\matx}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}_{\underline{r}}$ and $\Delta>0$. It holds that $\rank_\Delta\matx\leq\underline{r}$ for all $\matx\in B[\underline{\matx},\Delta]$.

issues.failure_explanation: The set $\{i:\sigma_{i+1}\leq\Delta\}$ can be empty when all singular values of $\matx$ are larger than $\Delta$ (or when $i=\min\{m,n\}$ and $\sigma_{i+1}$ is undefined). Thus $\rank_\Delta\matx$ is not defined for all matrices, making Proposition \ref{prop: rank delta} and the algorithms that use it ill-posed as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\rank_\Delta\matx$ as the number of singular values strictly greater than $\Delta$, or equivalently $\max\{i:\sigma_i>\Delta\}$ with the convention $\max\emptyset=0$.
issues.overall_effect: The definition and any result or algorithm relying on $\rank_\Delta$ (including the rank-decreasing index sets in Algorithms GRAP-R and rfGRAP-R) are not well-defined in the full-rank case.
issues.title: Delta-rank is ill-defined when all singular values exceed Delta
issues.why_classification: A short, local correction of the definition preserves all substantive claims and algorithms.

issues.failure_explanation: Expanding $\gamma(s)-(\tensX+s\tensV)$ using the tangent cone parametrization gives leading $s^2$ terms from $\tensC\times_k[\dot{\matu}_k\ 0]$ and $\tensG\times_j\dot{\matu}_j\times_k\dot{\matu}_k$, not $s^4$ terms as written. The displayed equality is false, so the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:added-1} is invalid as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the Taylor expansion to include the $s^2$ terms and adjust the constant $c(\tensX)$ accordingly; the lemma remains true but the proof must be repaired.
issues.overall_effect: The curvature bound in Lemma \ref{lem:added-1}, used to lower-bound the Armijo stepsize, is not established by the given proof.
issues.title: Incorrect Taylor expansion in curvature lemma
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial calculation error in a key technical lemma; the conclusion survives with a corrected argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The sum in the lower bound is over $k\in[d]\setminus I$, but the subsequent inequality used to bound the terms is stated for $k\in I$. The terms for $k\in I$ in the exact projection are not covered by this sum, so the final inequality $\geq \frac{c_I}{|I|+1}\|\proj_{\tangent_\tensX\!\tensM_{\leq\vecr}}\!\tensA\|_\frob^2$ is not justified as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing bound for the exact-projection terms with $k\in I$ (each can be bounded by $\|\tensA\times_{[d]\setminus I}\proj_{\matu_k}\|_\frob$) and combine with the $|I|+1$ factor.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the angle condition for the GRAP approximate projection is incomplete, so the guaranteed angle constant is not established by the given argument.
issues.title: Mismatched index set in angle-condition proof
issues.why_classification: A contained proof gap in a technical proposition; the intended result is repairable without changing the overall method.

issues.failure_explanation: The condition that the first term of the exact projection vanishes only says that $\nabla f$ is orthogonal to the tensor product of the subspaces $[\hat{\matu}_k\ \hat{\matu}_{k,1}^*]$ (for $k\in I$) and $\hat{\matu}_k$ (for $k\notin I$). It does not imply that the orthogonal projections $\proj^\perp_{[\hat{\matu}_k\ \hat{\matu}_{k,1}^*]}$ or $\proj^\perp_{\hat{\matu}_k}$ can be dropped in the remaining terms. The displayed equality therefore does not follow, and the lower bound on $\|\tensV_{\tensX_{\underline{\vecr}}}\|_\frob$ used to prove the sufficient decrease is unsupported for points where multiple modes are rank-deficient but not all.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a valid lower bound for the exact projection norm in Case 3 that correctly accounts for the orthogonal projections, or restrict the convergence proof to cases where the first term is nonzero; otherwise the analysis for partially rank-deficient points must be reworked.
issues.overall_effect: The sufficient decrease condition for GRAP-R is not established for the important class of partially rank-deficient accumulation points, so the claim that every accumulation point is stationary is not proven for such points.

issues.why_classification: The gap affects the central apocalypse-free guarantee for a broad class of rank-deficient points, and no simple local correction is evident; the main convergence theorem for GRAP-R is left unsupported for those points.
